To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Planck HFI maps of polarized dust emission show a high polarization fraction (up to 19.8%) in regions of moderate column density (N_(H) < 2 ×10^(21)cm^(-2)), a large scatter in polarization fraction at N_H below 10^(21), a decrease in polarization fraction with increasing N_H above 10^(21).

the polarization of dust is high, that there is a general decrease of dust polarization fraction with N_H and a sharp drop for N_H > 1.5 x 10^22 cm^-2, and that there is an anti-correlation between the dispersion of polarization angle and the polarization fraction.

(a) the polarization of Galactic dust emission is observed on a wide range of scales; (b) the maximum observed polarization fraction is high; (c) the dust polarization fraction is found not to depend on the dust optical depth; (d) the dust polarization is correlated with the magnetic field structure, and (e) the dust polarization does not correlate with the synchrotron emission.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the properties of dust polarization at large angular scales, which is a new field opened up by the Planck data.
understanding the origin of the polarization of the Galactic dust emission and the origin of the spatial structures of the polarization angle.
a detailed study of the properties of the polarized emission at 353 GHz and their implications for the properties of the magnetic field and dust grains in the interstellar medium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polarization properties of Galactic dust emission are complex and cannot be understood with a single simple model.
the polarization properties of the dust in the diffuse interstellar medium are not well understood, even at 1° scales.
the dust polarization fraction is a function of the magnetic field orientation, and the magnetic field orientation is a function of dust polarization fraction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Planck is the first all-sky survey to detect polarized thermal emission of Galactic dust, and that it has provided the first large-scale maps of the polarization fraction of thermal dust emission at high Galactic latitudes.
we are able to map the polarized emission from the thermal dust in the Milky Way, which is the first time that this has been done at the resolution of a degree.

the polarization fraction of thermal dust emission is a function of column density and magnetic field strength and orientation, and that the polarization angle dispersion is related to the strength and spatial fluctuations in the magnetic-field strength.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the polarization properties of Galactic dust are complex.
Planck has provided a unique view on dust polarization, which opens new avenues for studies of the magnetic field structure and of dust grain alignment in our Galaxy.
the Planck Hﬁ polarization data allow us to study dust polarization on large scales and to characterize the polarization of dust emission in the interstellar medium.
